text:
Alex W: Hey team — planning to provision a new GPU node pool for training jobs in us-west1. Question on the Terraform change: we want a mix of committed capacity + spot fallback. Also need to wire the instance profile secret and a KMS-wrapped bootstrap key. Can someone sanity-check the approach?
Mia C: sounds good. Do you have a proposal for how to split committed vs spot? e.g., 4 reserved nodes + autoscale spot up to 16?
Alex W: thinking 4 reserved (for stable throughput) + spot burst to 12. TF will create a node pool resource with capacityReservation for the reserved nodes and `preemptible`/spot for the rest. Need to make sure the IAM service account for the nodes can access the KMS key and the SSM-style secret.
Ryan (SRE): two quick things: 1) ensure capacityReservationGroup is set (GCP) or use "--reservation_id" for AWS. 2) mark reserved nodes with a label like `reserved=true` so workloads can prefer them.
Katie P: For GKE, we should avoid mixing preemptible and non-preemptible in same node pool. Instead do two node pools: one `gpu-reserved` (no preemptible), one `gpu-spot` (preemptible=true). Simpler scheduling and tainting.
Liz I: Agree with Katie. Also recommend a taint on spot nodes: `dedicated=gpu:NoExecute` (or NoSchedule) and a toleration on training pods that can tolerate eviction. That keeps critical infra off spot nodes.
Alex W: Good call. Terraform snippet I'm planning: ```resource "google_container_node_pool" "gpu_reserved" { name = "gpu-reserved" node_config { machine_type = "n1-highmem-8" accelerators { type = "nvidia-tesla-v100" count = 1 } labels = { "pool" = "gpu-reserved" } service_account = var.gpu_node_sa } initial_node_count = 4 autoscaling { enabled = true min_node_count = 4 max_node_count = 8 } }``` 
Mia C: For spot pool: ```resource "google_container_node_pool" "gpu_spot" { name = "gpu-spot" node_config { preemptible = true } initial_node_count = 0 autoscaling { enabled = true min_node_count = 0 max_node_count = 12 } }```
Alex W: For credentials: we store the node bootstrap credentials in Secret Manager with KMS CMEK. TF will grant `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor` to the node service account. Any objections?
Ryan (SRE): make sure to use a short-lived credential flow if secrets are sensitive. Granting SecretManager access to node SA is ok if the secret is only bootstrap and rotated. Document rotation procedure.
Katie P: Also add the KMS decrypt permission on the node SA: `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter`. And add an IAM condition limiting access to the specific resource.
Liz I: On rolling updates: set `max_surge = 1` and `max_unavailable = 1` to avoid killing many GPUs simultaneously. Add a pod disruption budget for training controller.
Alex W: Thanks — probing one more: terraform plan vs apply order. We will create the SA + bindings first, then create node pools. Is there any race you foresee where GKE won't pick up SA IAM quickly?
Mia C: It's eventual consistency. Add a `null_resource` with a short sleep and an explicit `depends_on` the IAM bindings to give cloud IAM time to propagate. Ugly but pragmatic.
deploy-bot: terraform plan finished: 3 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy. (link: https://ci.internal/plan/7623)
Ryan (SRE): thumbs up. Also add monitoring alert for high preempt rate on `gpu-spot` nodes so we can auto-shift traffic back to reserved pool if >30% preemptions in 5m.
Alex W: I'll draft the PR with two node pools, the TF IAM blocks, and the null_resource pause. Will ping for review when ready.
Katie P: Ping me for the IAM bits. I'll look at the KMS/Secret Manager permissions.
Liz I: I'll add the PDB and taint/toleration docs in the repo.
Alex W: thanks all :thumbsup:
